findings.claim: The stated retraction of the standard hyperbolic inclusion is incorrectly normalized. With H the unscaled hyperbolic construction and c_B the forgetful Betti map, c_B H = 1 + ψ^{−1}, hence 2 id on K(Z)[1/2]^(+), not id. Thus the fibre sequence with the specified first map is not split by c_B itself.
findings.evidence: FGV, published §3.4, pp.254–255, describes the inclusion as hyperbolic and says that (3.5) is “canonically split” by the forgetful spectrum map. But §3.5, p.256, explicitly computes the hyperbolic/Betti–Hodge composite as (1 + ψ^{−1}, 0). Already on K_0(Z)[1/2] = Z[1/2], the class of Z maps under H to a symplectic rank-two module and under c_B to 2[Z]. Inverting 2 makes this composite invertible, not equal to the identity. Publisher PDF DOI 10.1007/s00222-022-01127-8; both pages visually checked.
findings.fix: Keep the fibre sequence and splitting existence. If its first arrow is the standard H on the positive eigensummand, give the retraction as (1/2)c_B. Alternatively keep c_B as projection and explicitly use (1/2)H as the summand inclusion; specify the identification with homotopy orbits accordingly. Amend item /25 and the route-3 design instruction, record this normalization issue in sourceIssues, and require the degree-zero test c_B(H([Z])) = 2[Z]. Theorem 3.5 and the universal-extension results are not contradicted.

findings.claim: The item promotes the adjoint Σ∞_+|C| → K(C) for an arbitrary symmetric monoidal groupoid to a ring map. One monoidal operation provides additive group completion, not a unital ring structure on K(C); the assertion needs a second compatible multiplicative structure or a specific multiplicative map into K(R).
findings.evidence: Published §2.2, pp.237–238, gives a spectrum and the group-completion map (2.2). §2.3, p.238, obtains products for commutative R from tensor product, distinct from direct sum. The ring-spectrum map on p.240 is specifically Σ∞_+|Pic(R)| → K(R), preserving tensor product, not the generic group-completion adjunction. Counterexample: let C be the discrete groupoid on Q/Z with addition. It is symmetric monoidal and already group-like, so π_0 K(C) = Q/Z. No nonzero unital ring has this additive group: if its unit has finite additive order n, every element is killed by n, whereas Q/Z has unbounded exponent. Also, using the sole operation as multiplication on Σ∞_+|C|, its unit [0] maps to additive zero under group completion.
findings.fix: Replace the general “adjoint ring maps” clause by “adjoint maps of spectra”. State multiplicativity separately for commutative-ring projectives with direct sum and tensor product, and for the Picard-groupoid map Σ∞_+|Pic(R)| → K(R) already in item /17. Do not claim K(Pic(R), tensor) is the codomain of that map. Preserve the existing general group-completion owner and place any required ring-product input with GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.7/SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.6; no new generic ring structure on every K(C).

findings.claim: After specifying the spaces of B∞X as |X(S^n)|, the item says specialness makes this an Ω-spectrum. Specialness supplies the Ω-equivalences only for n ≥ 1; the zero structure map is group completion and need not be a weak equivalence. The omitted qualification would erase the group completion that algebraic and symplectic K-theory require.
findings.evidence: Published Appendix A.1, p.302, explicitly restricts the weak equivalences (A.2) to n ≥ 1 and says B∞X is equivalent to an Ω-spectrum whose zeroth space is Ω|X(S^1)|, followed by the group-completion map (A.4). Take the special Γ-space X(S) = N^(S minus basepoint), with pointed maps acting by summation over fibres. Its Segal maps are isomorphisms, X({*}) is a point, and |X(S^0)| = N. Its zero structure map is N → ΩBN and on π_0 is N → Z, not a bijection. Thus it is not an Ω-spectrum at level zero. This example satisfies even the paper’s strict reduction condition, so it is separate from existing E15.
findings.fix: State that |X(S^n)| → Ω|X(S^(n+1))| is a weak equivalence for n ≥ 1. Give the Ω-spectrum replacement with zeroth space Ω|X(S^1)| and retain |X(S^0)| → Ω∞B∞X as group completion. If the unmodified prespectrum is claimed to be an Ω-spectrum also at zero, add that π_0 X(S^0) is a group (very specialness). Carry the N-to-Z test into the H.4/H.5 design contract. The source itself gives the correct distinction; this finding is an extraction error, not a new published-source error.
